title: POC scoping - workload modeling - Crestline Financial
summary: Discovery / POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modelling. Customer uses LLM for payments NLP routing and transaction summarization; typical flow is short input (avg ~30-60 tokens) and longer outputs (avg ~110-180 tokens). They want a 4-week pilot to validate cost & latency targets. Success criteria: p95 latency <200ms for inference path, <2% error rate, acceptable cost per 1M tokens vs their current on-prem baseline. Action items: send SOW + pricing, run benchmark harness (10k requests with peak shaping), share security docs and benchmark scripts.
next_steps: Alex Chen - send SOW and pricing for 4-week pilot (including Dedicated and hosted options) by 2027-03-12
Priya Kapoor - provide benchmark harness and seed script + sample data by 2027-03-11
Crestline - share production traffic sample (anonymized) and peak days by 2027-03-10
Schedule kickoff benchmark run week of 2027-03-15
action_items: Priya Kapoor: upload benchmark harness & sample workload scripts to shared drive (due 2027-03-11)
John Mallory: export 7 days of anonymized traffic (due 2027-03-10)
Mike Harrington: confirm security/contract owner and provide contact for SOC2 review (due 2027-03-14)
transcript: 00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to run through the workload modelling for the poc — real quick intros. 00:06 John Mallory: John here, eng lead at Crestline. we run transaction NLP and routing, mostly to classify transactions and generate merchant summaries. 00:14 Alex Chen: Great, Priya from our infra/SE team will lead the QPS and token discussion. 00:18 Priya Kapoor: hey all — quick note, i'm going to ask about peak qps, concurrency, and token distributions so we can size the pilot and recommend dedicated vs hosted. 00:27 Sara Velez: our common flow: user submits a short description or phone receipt, so inputs are small — median input ~32 tokens, 90th perc ~120 tokens. outputs are larger because we synthesize a paragraph — median output ~110 tokens, 95th ~340, tail up to ~1k tokens but that's rare. 00:46 Priya Kapoor: helpful — what's your current traffic shape? avg qps, peak qps, and concurrency? 00:52 Mike Harrington: avg qps around 18 during weekdays, peak burst observed at 120 qps during payroll windows, concurrency around 6-10 for the inference service. we do occasional spikes up to ~180 for short windows. 01:07 Priya Kapoor: ok that's useful. for a 4-week pilot we usually run a benchmark that simulates typical diurnal traffic + a couple peak bursts. we'll want to mimic your 120-180 qps bursts to see latency+errors. 01:19 John Mallory: latency is critical — we need p95 under 200ms for the routing path, ideally p99 <500ms. cost target is also important — our finance team set a soft target of reducing per-request inference cost vs our on-prem baseline by at least 30%. 01:33 Priya Kapoor: we can try two configs: hosted with optimized batching and local cache, and Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) with KV cache primed. Dedicated usually gives lower tail latency for these bursty loads. 01:45 Alex Chen: quick clarification — when you say routing path, is that the full end-to-end including our pre/post-processing and your orchestration, or strictly model infer? 01:52 Sara Velez: ideally model infer p95 <200ms; end-to-end can be slightly higher but we want predictability. 01:58 Priya Kapoor: got it. for model infer numbers, expect p50/p95/p99 to depend a lot on batching and sequence length. With median input 32 + median output 110 — the total token context is ~142 tokens which is quite friendly. 02:12 Priya Kapoor: rough sizing: if you sustain 50 qps of model calls with average 142 tokens total, that's about 426k tokens per minute, roughly 25.5M tokens per hour — sorry, math slip: actually per minute it would be 50 qps * 142 tokens = 7,100 tokens/sec -> 426k tokens/min -> about 25.6M tokens/hr, yes. 02:32 Mike Harrington: whoa, ok that scales. we mostly average lower but the bursts matter. 02:37 Priya Kapoor: for pilot benchmarking we'll run three phases: baseline low qps ramp, daytime steady, and burst tests that hit 120 and 180 qps for 5-10 minute windows. total benchmark test set will be ~10k requests to get stable latency stats. 02:50 Alex Chen: we'll also capture concurrency and queueing behavior and show token cost estimates for each config. 02:55 John Mallory: what about caching? some requests are repeats — can you illustrate KV cache gains? 03:00 Priya Kapoor: yes — prefix/KV cache can reduce compute for repeated prefixes; for your use-case where users often submit semantically similar receipts, we typically see effective token savings of 10-25% on repeated flows after warm-up. caching also reduces p95 during bursts because fewer forward passes needed. 03:18 Sara Velez: ok good. will you run the benchmark against both hosted and dedicated so we can compare? 03:22 Priya Kapoor: yes, we'll run hosted config with intelligent batching and streaming disabled for fairness, and then Dedicated with larger batch windows and primed KV cache. 03:31 Priya Kapoor: one more: what are your availability/SLA expectations for the pilot? 03:35 Mike Harrington: we need 99.5% availability for the inference path during pilot, and automated retry policies for 5xxs. 03:42 Alex Chen: noted. security questions? 03:44 John Mallory: we'll need SOC2 docs, encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS for the Dedicated option, RBAC and audit log export. 03:53 Priya Kapoor: we have SOC2 and can support KMS/HSM integrations for Private/Dedicated; we'll share the security packet. 03:59 Sara Velez: timeline: if we sign SOW this week, can you start benchmarks by March 15? 04:04 Alex Chen: target yes — priya will upload harness and sample scripts by March 11, then kickoff week of March 15. 04:09 Priya Kapoor: benchmark metrics we'll capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, effective tokens served, and cost per 1M tokens estimate. 04:20 Mike Harrington: for success criteria let's be explicit: model infer p95 <200ms, error rate <2% during simulated peaks, and cost per 1M tokens not exceeding our target (we'll supply their current baseline numbers). 04:33 John Mallory: also include a qualitative check — output quality must match or exceed our current LM in recall for merchant info (we'll provide evaluation prompts and acceptance thresholds). 04:43 Priya Kapoor: perfect — we'll run eval set of ~500 prompts and report BLEU/ROUGE-ish numbers plus manual spot checks. 04:51 Alex Chen: any blockers on contracts or procurement? 04:54 Mike Harrington: procurement will need standard terms and proof of SOC2; legal wants a clause about data residency for EU customers. 04:59 Alex Chen: noted, i'll include legal/ps contact in SOW. 05:03 John Mallory: quick note on traffic shape: 30% of calls are short summary flows (input <20 tokens, output ~40-80 tokens), 60% are mid-length (input 20-80, output ~80-180), 10% are long tail. 05:18 Priya Kapoor: that distribution helps to size batching windows; short flows do well with smaller batch latency budgets, mids can be batched more aggressively. 05:27 Sara Velez: do you have a sample benchmark spreadsheet we can look at? 05:30 Alex Chen: yes, we will share the benchmark spreadsheet + example CSV for the harness (link posted in chat: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/crestline-poc — note: internal link, access tbd). 05:40 Mike Harrington: what's the expected pilot cost range? 05:42 Alex Chen: rough back-of-envelope: for Dedicated 2 GPUs with reserved throughput we estimate $Xk/month for the pilot traffic profile; hosted per-token will vary but we will provide exact cost estimates after the first benchmark run. we'll include both in the SOW. 05:56 John Mallory: ok wrap-up — good alignment on metrics and timeline. 06:00 Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with SOW, harness, and security docs. 06:05 (call end)
notes: Transcript contains occasional auto-transcription errors and imperfect punctuation.
Benchmark plan: 10k requests across phases (ramp, steady, burst).
Pilot length proposed: 4 weeks (benchmark + 2-week soak + evaluation).
